subject: Post-call: SprintBridge pilot — scope, risks, and next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Avery Nolan <avery.nolan@sprintbridge.com>, Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@sprintbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: SprintBridge pilot — scope, risks, and next steps

Hi Avery / Jordan —

Thanks again for a productive conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into procurement and security review. If anything below is off, please flag and we’ll update the MPA.

What you told us (pain & goals)
- Latency-sensitive inference in control plane logs: current vendor causes 350–500ms tail latency for web callbacks during peak.
- Cost: unpredictable per-token billing across different models — needs predictable unit economics for pilot.
- Data residency & audit: security team requires VPC + audit logs for any production integration.

Pilot objective (agreed scope)
- 6-week pilot to validate inference latency reduction and <150ms median for representative traffic; cost comparison vs current provider.
- Use case: realtime customer-facing chat + nightly batch reranking for recommendations.
- Success metrics: median latency <150ms, 30% per-token cost reduction in steady-state, and passes security checklist for controlled data flows.

Milestones & tentative timeline (please confirm dates)
1) Sandbox access & baseline run (Redwood provides test model endpoints) — target: 2026-09-10
2) Integration + smoke tests (SprintBridge engineering) — target: 2026-09-17
3) Security review complete (SprintBridge security + Redwood security artifacts) — target: 2026-09-24
4) Pilot start / production-like run — target: 2026-09-28
5) Wrap & decision: metrics review + next steps — target: 2026-10-12

Key stakeholders (who needs to be involved)
- SprintBridge: Avery Nolan (product), Jordan Patel (engineering), Procurement (procurement@sprintbridge.com), Security reviewer (TBD)
- Redwood: Kimberly Park (seller), Ben Carter (solutions), Soojin Lee (security lead)

Open questions we flagged on the call
- Will SprintBridge accept Redwood hosted endpoints behind a private VPC peering for the pilot, or do you require on-prem for sample traffic?
- Procurement: what is your standard PO timeline and who should we loop in for SOW review?
- Security artifacts: we’ll share SOC2 summary, network diagrams, and audit-log examples — who is the primary recipient?

Attachments: I’ve attached an initial Mutual Action Plan (MPA) and a draft SOW with the scope and baseline SLAs. I updated milestone dates based on our call — see column "SprintBridge proposed date" in the MPA.

Ask / next steps
- Can you confirm the stakeholder list above and the proposed dates by EOD Tuesday (2026-09-01)?
- If procurement needs a redline SOW or specific billing terms, please send the contact and we’ll prioritize.

Thanks — we’ll stand up sandbox endpoints this week and Ben will share the integration checklist.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments:
- SprintBridge_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.xlsx (MPA: milestones, owners, dates)
- SOW-draft-Redwood-2026.docx (scope + baseline pricing)

From: Avery Nolan <avery.nolan@sprintbridge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@sprintbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: SprintBridge pilot — scope, risks, and next steps

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick notes and one ask: we like the proposed milestones but need to shift the security review window by one week to allow internal calendar constraints.

Changes we need
- Security review completion to 2026-10-01 instead of 2026-09-24. Security has a standing audit on 09/22 that blocks their availability that week.
- Procurement: we are fast-tracking, but they need an estimated monthly cost range for a 3-node reserved pool — can Redwood provide a ballpark (USD) for pilot vs projected monthly if we convert to reserved capacity?

Questions
- Is VPC peering required for the pilot, or can we run in a private-hosted sandbox with IP allowlist first?
- Who at Redwood will own the SOC2 / diagram packet? My security lead is Samir (samir.khan@sprintbridge.com) — please CC him on the artifacts.

I’ll check with Procurement and loop in procurement@sprintbridge.com with any PO timeline updates.

Thanks,
Avery
Product Lead, SprintBridge
avery.nolan@sprintbridge.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Avery Nolan <avery.nolan@sprintbridge.com>, Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@sprintbridge.com>, procurement@sprintbridge.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@sprintbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Updated MPA + cost estimates for reserved capacity (pilot estimates)

Avery / Jordan / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick reply and for identifying the security calendar conflict. I’ve updated the MPA (attached) to reflect the shifted security review target of 2026-10-01. Highlights and answers below.

1) VPC & sandbox options- We can start with a hosted sandbox behind an IP allowlist for smoke tests (no peering required). For the pilot production-like run we recommend VPC peering to match your security requirements; both paths are supported.

2) Cost estimates (pilot) — rough ranges for planning only- Hosted sandbox (on-demand): ~ $1,600–$2,400 / week (3-node equivalent, burstable)- Pilot reserved (monthly committed 3 GPUs, quantized model): ~ $8,000–$10,000 / month
These are ballpark estimates; Ben will provide a more precise breakdown by token class and expected QPS after we have your traffic profile.

3) Owners & decision process (updated)- SprintBridge: Avery Nolan (product owner), Jordan Patel (engineering owner), Procurement (PO + SOW sign-off), Samir Khan (security approver)- Redwood: Kimberly Park (commercial lead), Ben Carter (integration/solutions), Soojin Lee (security contact)
Decision route: Security review -> Procurement PO -> SOW sign-off -> Pilot activation

4) Updated milestone table (MPA, key rows pasted)
- Sandbox access: Redwood provides credentials and sample traffic generator — target 2026-09-10 — owner: Ben Carter (Redwood) / Jordan Patel (SprintBridge)
- Integration + smoke tests: target 2026-09-17 — owner: Jordan Patel
- Security review complete: target 2026-10-01 — owner: Samir Khan / Soojin Lee
- Pilot start (prod-like): target 2026-10-05 — owner: Ben Carter / Jordan Patel
- Metrics review & decision: target 2026-10-19 — owner: Avery Nolan / Kimberly Park

5) Next asks from us- Please confirm: (A) that Samir is the primary security contact and (B) that procurement@sprintbridge.com is the correct procurement email.
- If you can share an expected QPS profile (peak and p50/p90 latencies) by EOD Thursday (2026-09-02), Ben will produce a token-cost estimate and a recommended batch/quantization profile.

I’ve attached the updated MPA file (v1.1) and a lightly redlined SOW with baseline pricing so procurement has something to review. If procurement prefers, we can prepare a short 1-page commercial summary for fast PO approval.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments:
- SprintBridge_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.xlsx (updated v1.1: dates + owners)
- SOW-draft-Redwood-2026.docx (light redlines)

From: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@sprintbridge.com>

Cc: procurement@sprintbridge.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Updated MPA + cost estimates for reserved capacity (pilot estimates)

Kim / Avery —

Thanks — Jordan here. Confirming we can target the updated dates (security to 10/01, pilot start 10/05). I’ll send a short QPS snapshot by tomorrow morning so Ben has something to work with.

Procurement: we’ll route the SOW to procurement@sprintbridge.com and expect a 7–10 business day review once the packet lands — I’ll follow up with a PO contact.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on estimates.

—Jordan
Senior Engineering Manager, SprintBridge
jordan.patel@sprintbridge.com | +1 (978) 555-0170
